title: Elliptic L-series Acb kernel
objective: Generalize the completed central Mellin grid into a batched moderate-complex Acb value kernel with honest diagnostics

oracles: Reference split-Mellin evaluator, Sage/PARI, and existing central derivative jet
exceptions: Handwritten C is the existing FLINT/Acb host adapter and bulk complex numerical primitive; ordinary Python remains the correctness fallback

handoff.summary: Implemented the shared split-Mellin Acb batch evaluator and N-API adapter with canonical raw/completed normalization, explicit nonrigorous diagnostics and resource limits, and focused Sage/PARI, functional-equation, parity, trivial-zero, and high-precision oracle tests.
risks: Trapezoidal discretization is intentionally not enclosed, so every returned value remains explicitly nonrigorous even when the known coefficient, local-grid, and outer-tail target is met.

The full native suite passes all executable tests but its native-export inventory gate fails until the integration lane registers and classifies sagejs_ec_lseries_values; that shared inventory is outside this lane's claims.
Heights above 100, real offsets above 8, and resource plans exceeding the declared operation limits are rejected by design.
next_steps: Register ecLseriesValues in addon.c, consume the documented top-level and per-point schema, update shared native architecture inventories and audit hashes, and rerun the integrated native suite.
Run the integrated API and oracle corpus on Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64, and Windows x64.
